task1.title: Frequency of eating at fast food restaurants in the USA, 2003–2013
task1.prompt: The chart below shows how frequently people in the USA ate in fast food restaurants between 2003 and 2013.

chartDesc.title: Frequency of eating at fast food restaurants among people in the USA (2003–2013)
chartDesc.overview: Eating fast food 'Once a week' or 'Once or twice a month' were consistently the most common frequencies (accounting for around 25%–33% each), while eating 'Every day' or 'Never' were the least common across all three years (5% or less).
keyFeatures: In 2003 and 2006, 'Once a week' was the highest category at 31% and 33% respectively, but it declined to 28% in 2013.
'Once or twice a month' peaked in 2013 at 33%, becoming the highest overall proportion in that year.
The proportion of people eating fast food 'Every day' and 'Never' consistently remained lowest, under 5% throughout the entire period.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

task2.title: Fast trains versus improving existing public transport
task2.prompt:
In a number of countries, some people think it is necessary to spend large sums of money on constructing new railway lines for very fast trains between cities. Others believe the money should be spent on improving existing public transport.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
